commands.review_summary:
The PR changes Discord tail processing so event-scoped handler errors, panics, and timeouts are logged with safe event metadata without stopping the tail, while queue saturation remains fatal.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main forwards any worker handler error through the fatal channel, and the PR's closed-store test demonstrates the proposed continuation path. A live Discord/store reproduction was not supplied, but the failure transition is explicit in code.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A maintainer must define the acceptable escalation policy for systemic or repeated handler failures before the branch can be safely repaired or merged.

target.title: fix: keep tail alive after handler failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A single Discord Gateway event handler error, recovered panic, or cooperative 30-second timeout was sent through the same fatal channel as worker-queue saturation. That terminated `discrawl tail`, even though the Gateway session itself was healthy, and the returned error lacked the event type and identifiers needed to diagnose the failed event.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Separate fatal tail failures from event-scoped handler failures; queue saturation remains fail-fast.
- Carry safe event metadata through queued work and report handler errors, panics, and timeouts without terminating the tail.
- Route structured warnings through the existing syncer logger with event type, failure kind, and available guild/channel/message/user IDs.
- Propagate metadata learned by both client-side and syncer-side message-update refetches without adding another Discord REST fetch.
- Keep missing handlers, Gateway/session open failures, ready-hook failures, cancellation, worker bounds, and shutdown behavior unchanged.

## User Impact

Transient per-event database or Discord failures no longer stop the live tail. Later events continue processing, while warnings identify which event failed without logging message content, payloads, usernames, tokens, panic values, or raw secret-bearing errors. A saturated worker queue still terminates the tail so dropped events are not hidden.

## Evidence

- `go test -count=1 ./...`
- `go test -count=1 -race ./...`
- Focused continuation, refetch-metadata, queue-full, and ready-failure tests repeated 10 times
- Filtered coverage: `85.1%` against the `85.0%` floor
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2`, `go vet`, `staticcheck v0.7.0`, `deadcode v0.47.0`, `gofumpt v0.10.0`, and `gosec v2.27.1`
- `go mod verify`, tidy diff, `govulncheck v1.5.0`, build, CLI smoke tests, and GoReleaser snapshot checks
- Independent concurrency review and race/checkptr verification found no required issues
